record.paper_title: Ductile-to-brittle transition and yielding in soft amorphous materials: perspectives and open questions
record.original_question: Does the ductile-to-brittle transition in soft amorphous materials occur at a critical value of a parameter that controls system rigidity, and is this transition underlain by a dynamical non-equilibrium phase transition?

evidence.quote: However, it is not yet clear whether the DBT occurs at some critical value of the parameter controlling the system rigidity , i.e., in the language of non-equilibrium statistical mechanics, whether there exists a (dynamical) phase transition underlying DBT.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a soft amorphous material (e.g., a foam, emulsion, colloidal glass, or model athermal glass) subjected to quasistatic shear deformation. Empirically, depending on a control parameter that governs the rigidity/stability of the system (such as the degree of annealing of the initial configuration, the density, or a related preparation parameter), the macroscopic stress–strain response at yielding can range from a sharp, discontinuous "brittle" stress drop to a smooth, continuous "ductile" flow. Let p denote this rigidity-control parameter.

Questions:
(a) Does there exist a critical value p_c of the rigidity-control parameter p such that the ductile-to-brittle transition (DBT) occurs precisely at p = p_c, in the sense that the qualitative character of the yielding response changes singularly at p_c?
(b) If such a p_c exists, is the DBT underlain by a genuine non-equilibrium (dynamical) phase transition — that is, can one define an order parameter and identify singular behavior (e.g., diverging correlation length, scaling, universality) at p_c in the thermodynamic limit, in the language of non-equilibrium statistical mechanics?

Provide a proof, a definitive theoretical argument, or a counterexample.
artifact.category_tag: Non-equilibrium phase transitions in amorphous solids
artifact.status_search_result: There is substantial recent evidence supporting the existence of a critical point underlying the DBT. Ozawa et al. (PNAS 2018) identified a random critical point — in the universality class of the random-field Ising model — separating brittle and ductile yielding in athermal amorphous solids as the degree of annealing varies. Follow-up work (e.g., mean-field analyses beyond RFIM, 2024; finite-disorder critical point with aspherical impurities, 2026; activity-induced annealing studies in Nature Physics 2024) refines and extends this picture. However, full consensus on universality class, the precise nature of the dynamical phase transition, and the role of finite-dimensional fluctuations and microscopic details is not yet established, so the question is best regarded as partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Random critical point separates brittle and ductile yielding transitions in amorphous materials
status_evidence.snippet: Yielding terminates in a second-order critical point in the universality class of an Ising model in a random field as annealing decreases.
status_evidence.claim: A random critical point separating brittle and ductile yielding has been identified, supporting the existence of an underlying non-equilibrium phase transition.

status_evidence.title: Ductile and brittle yielding of athermal amorphous solids: A mean-field paradigm beyond the random-field Ising model
status_evidence.snippet: Mean-field analysis of ductile and brittle yielding extending beyond RFIM.
status_evidence.claim: Theoretical extensions beyond RFIM continue to refine the picture of the DBT as a critical phenomenon, indicating the question is partially but not fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: Finite Disorder Critical Point in Brittle-to-Ductile Transition in Amorphous Solids with Aspherical Impurities
status_evidence.snippet: Identifies a finite-disorder critical point in the brittle-to-ductile transition.
status_evidence.claim: Further critical-point structure of the DBT has been characterized in extended models.

status_evidence.title: Activity-induced annealing leads to a ductile-to-brittle transition in amorphous solids
status_evidence.snippet: Activity-induced annealing drives a DBT in amorphous solids.
status_evidence.claim: Additional control parameters that drive the DBT have been identified, consistent with a critical-transition picture but with open questions on universality.
